sections.h2: Where is Walker County and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Walker County sits in the far northwest corner of Georgia, next to Hamilton County, Tennessee, and is part of the Chattanooga metro area. The General Assembly created it on December 18, 1833, from land that had belonged to the Cherokee Nation, and LaFayette is the county seat, per Wikipedia.

The county covers 447 square miles of ridges, caves and coves. Lookout Mountain, Pigeon Mountain, McLemore Cove and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest all fall inside its lines, which means a house here can be a village lot in LaFayette, a hillside place near Lookout Mountain, or acreage in the valleys. Catoosa, Whitfield, Gordon, Floyd, Chattooga and Dade counties touch its other borders, along with DeKalb County, Alabama.

Four of the five county commission seats are tied to districts named for Rossville, Chickamauga, LaFayette and Lookout Mountain, a useful map of where the population clusters. Rossville and Chickamauga also carry Civil War history from the autumn 1863 Chickamauga Campaign.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Walker County homes?
sections.html:
Most Walker County homes are owner-occupied, and values sit well under the national figure. The table below comes from the Census Bureau QuickFacts page.

The county counted 67,654 residents in the 2020 census, a dip from 68,756 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate shows a 3.8% rise over the 2020 base. In 2020 about 28.2% of occupied units were rented, and 10.1% of all units stood vacant. That rental and vacancy mix is why investor buyers show up for tired houses here.

sections.h2: Which Walker County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The Tax Commissioner bills and collects; the Board of Tax Assessors values property and approves exemptions.

  • Rock Spring office: 122 Highway 95 (mail to P O Box 510, Rock Spring, GA 30739), 706-638-2929, Monday to Friday 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M., drop box by the main entrance.
  • Rossville office: 2012 McFarland Gap Road, Rossville, GA 30741, same phone and hours.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 706-638-4823, the number the commissioner's site gives for preferential assessment questions.
  • Online lookup and payment: walkercountytax.com.

The county site states that the commissioner's office does not set values or the tax rate. For the mill rate on your bill, read the levy lines for the county and the school system, or ask the office to explain them.

sections.h2: When is Walker County property tax due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due 60 days after the bills are mailed, which the county says is December 20 in most years. Georgia's default due date is also December 20, and a county may move it earlier by resolution, so the date printed on your bill controls.

Mailed payments are accepted on a United States Postal Service postmark, and metered postage marks do not count. The state allows 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest accrues, then penalties can follow on unpaid balances.

  • Mobile and manufactured homes in the county on January 1 are taxed by April 1, with a 10% penalty plus 1% per month interest if unpaid, and a possible citation to State Court or sale of the home.
  • Tax is figured on the property owned on January 1, so a buyer who closes later in the year may need to ask the office to redirect the bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Walker County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed to file a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors. The appeal can challenge taxability, value or uniformity with similar properties, and it cannot be based on a complaint about the size of the tax bill.

The assessors review first. If they do not agree, the file moves to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing, and a further appeal can go to Superior Court. Arbitration is offered in place of the Board of Equalization, and the assessors can explain how it works. A taxpayer who disagrees with the existing value can also file a new return between January 1 and April 1, which begins the same appeal track if the board rejects the figure.

Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value unless a law says otherwise (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7), so the assessed value on your notice is smaller than the market value.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs apply in Walker County?
sections.html:
Walker County lists both state and local homestead exemptions on its tax site, and the larger of the local or state amount applies. First-time homeowners should bring a copy of the warranty deed when applying.

  • Regular state homestead: printed on the county page as $2,000 for state, school and county purposes, for owners who live in the home on January 1.
  • Local senior exemptions: owners 70 and older with a $15,000 adjusted gross income limit can claim a county-tax exemption, and the county school tax exemptions start at 70 and 75.
  • Disabled veterans and surviving spouses: the page prints $81,080 for the disabled veteran and armed forces surviving spouse exemptions.
  • Deferral: owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less may defer payment until ownership changes or deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value.
  • 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant: an $18,000 reduction in assessed value used to figure a credit, available when a homestead exemption was filed by April 1, 2026, and shown directly on the 2026 bill.

The homestead deadline is April 1 each year, and later applications roll to the next tax year. Rental houses and investment property do not qualify for the grant.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Walker County house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff, and have the closing agent pay it from your proceeds. Georgia lets a county levy on and sell property when tax stays unpaid, so a balance does not go away at closing.

If the house sits outside LaFayette or Rossville, check whether the parcel is a mobile home, since those bills fall due April 1 and carry their own penalty. Houses that were inherited, rented out or left empty can have several years open, so ask for each year's status in writing. With about one home in four rented in 2020, buyers who purchase as-is are common, and a cash sale can pay the county from the sale funds without repairs or listing steps.

If you bought after January 1, make sure the bill is in your name so no reminder goes to the prior owner.

faqs.q: When are Walker County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Sixty days after the bills are mailed, which the county says is December 20 in most years. Check the date printed on your bill, because a county can change it.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Walker County bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at 706-638-2929 for billing and payments. The Rock Spring and Rossville offices are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. For value questions, the Board of Tax Assessors is at 706-638-4823.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Walker County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, which reviews first and then sends the appeal to the Board of Equalization if no agreement is reached.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a homestead exemption in Walker County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Commissioner's office, with the deadline set at April 1. A first-time applicant should carry the warranty deed. Once granted, the exemption renews on its own unless your residence or ownership changes.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Walker County house if taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and the closing agent pays it from the proceeds. Ask the office for the status of every past year if the house was a rental or an inherited property.
